annotation.title_clean: Redefining Safety in Light of Human-Robot Interaction: A Critical Review of Current Standards and Regulations
annotation.title_en: Redefining Safety in Light of Human-Robot Interaction: A Critical Review of Current Standards and Regulations
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Martinetti, A.; Chemweno, P.K.; Nizamis, K.; Fosch-Villaronga, E.
named_instruments_referenced: EU Civil Law Rules on Robotics 2017
annotation.summary_en: Critical review of EU regulations and ISO standards on robot safety, arguing that safety must be redefined beyond physical harm to include interaction (physical and social), psychosocial, cybersecurity, temporal and societal dimensions as robots integrate AI and machine learning.
key_provisions_or_claims: Traditional safety definitions focus narrowly on physical harm and separate robots from humans.
Safety should include psychosocial aspects such as mental health, trust, anthropomorphisation and technostress.
Cybersecurity must be part of safety for connected, cloud-linked robots.
Machine learning requires evolving, temporal safety mechanisms as robots change over time.
Standards and regulations proceed separately; a joint approach is needed, including for the proposed EU Machinery Regulation.
